title: A gate blocks a legitimate path: what do you change?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Gate blocks a valid customer group, proof exists in tool data
Same, but an occasional slip is acceptable
Proof needs something tools can't see (photo ID)
Agent skips verification on normal accounts
Instructions have a non-zero failure rate
Hook blocks and redirects to escalation
rule: Don't weaken a gate to fix its blind spot. Teach the gate a second kind of proof, in code.

title: Customer raises several things: how do you organise the work?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Several small concerns, one or two calls each
Several concerns, each a long independent investigation
Need one view of the facts
Agent ends early on a single concern
Text is a poor completion signal
Escalate that item, finish the others
rule: Decompose the request into a list and finish every item. Use subagents only when each item is heavy enough to need its own context.

title: Handing work to a human: what do they need first?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Human must act; time goes on what was tried and why it stopped
Long chat, recent turns matter most
Human has no transcript at all
rule: A handoff should tell the next person what was tried, what blocked it and what to do now. Keep the transcript as backup, not as the handoff.

title: A rule about what Claude may do: which mechanism?
head: Kind of rule
Mechanism
Enforced?
rows: Allow or deny by tool, path or command
Depends on the content of the call (amount, field, diff)
A personal preference only for you
rule: Guidance (CLAUDE.md) is not enforcement. For path and command limits, use permission rules; reach for a hook when the rule depends on content.

title: Need a tool to run? Which control actually guarantees it?
head: Requirement
Mechanism
Limit
rows: A specific tool must run first
Model must call some tool, not write text
Block a call until a prerequisite ran
Model often picks the wrong similar tool
Policy limit on an action (e.g. refund cap)
rule: Hooks stop wrong calls; they don't cause right ones. If a specific tool must run first, force it with tool_choice.

title: Information crosses between agent and human: in what form?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Agent → human, human lacks the transcript
Structured summary: ID, root cause, amount, action
Human → agent, decisions in free-text shorthand
Resolution fields in the same record, loaded as case facts
Human → agent, decisions already structured in a system
Give the agent a read tool for it
Returning customer, facts lost between contacts
Fresh session with a structured summary
rule: Handoffs go both ways. Bring the human's decision back in structured fields the agent loads with its case facts.

title: Must-hold rule: where does the code sit?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Code computes a flag the agent reads
Action must be blocked above a limit
Step B must wait for step A
Need a second view of an extraction
rule: Financial controls can't rely on the agent choosing to comply. Block the outgoing call in code until the condition is met.

title: A required step gets skipped: what kind of control matches the rule?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: A step must happen before a risky action, every time, for each item
PreToolUse hook / prerequisite gate on the risky call
Checks at the moment of action, keyed to the item
One specific tool must run first, once, before anything else
Controls a single turn, not later ordering
Model must call some tool instead of replying in text
Guarantees a tool call, not which or when
Model picks the wrong tool among similar ones
Tool output is messy or in mixed formats
rule: Put the check where the risk is: on the risky call, keyed to the thing being acted on. tool_choice decides one turn, not an ordering rule.

title: Customer issues go missing: when are they lost?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Several issues in one message; first reply covers only one
Split into concerns, investigate in parallel, answer together
Issues acknowledged, then forgotten many turns later
Facts fading in a long context
Case-facts block at the top of each prompt
Human picking up an escalation lacks context
Structured handoff summary (ID, root cause, amount, action)
Persist transactional facts outside the summary
Concerns are independent and slow to look up
Parallel tool calls with shared context
rule: If issues are lost in the first reply, fix decomposition. If they are lost many turns later, fix memory.

title: Handing over work: who picks it up, and what do they read?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Human takes over, won't read the transcript
Same person continues tomorrow in Claude Code
Context nearly full, same session continues
rule: When a human takes over, hand them a short structured summary, not the session.

title: What does the next person need from the agent?
head: Situation
Right artefact
Why
rows: Human takes over without the transcript
Deciding which items go to review
Keeps facts from being summarised away
Structured summary in a fresh session
rule: When handing work to a human without the transcript, send a short structured brief: what, where, what was tried, what you recommend.

title: Prompt or code? Ask what one miss costs
head: Requirement
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Step that must happen every time before an action
Prompts have a non-zero failure rate
Hard limit on an action (e.g. refund ceiling)
Model must call some tool instead of replying
Tone or format varies between chats
rule: Code for must-always; prompt and examples for should-usually.

title: A required step is sometimes skipped: words or code?
head: Requirement
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Step must precede another on every run (compliance)
Programmatic gate on the downstream tool
Coordinator should aim for a quality bar
Goals and quality criteria in its prompt
Output format or judgement is inconsistent
Fresh eyes, but runs after generation
rule: Must happen every time means code. A prompt can raise the odds but can't guarantee the order.

title: Something must happen before something else: what enforces it?
head: Requirement
Mechanism
Coverage
rows: Must never be skipped, many items per session
Programmatic gate / hook on the downstream tool
One specific tool must run first, single-item request
Model must call some tool, not answer in text
Block an action above a threshold
rule: Must-never rules need code on every call. Forced tool_choice shapes one request, not a whole session.
